title: Applications of Newton's Laws & Gravitation
summary: Applying Newton's laws covers friction, uniform circular motion, and universal gravitation. Friction is $f=\mu N$; circular motion needs centripetal force $F_c=mv^2/r$; gravity is $F=Gm_1m_2/r^2$.

friction.in_class: $f=\mu N$; static (up to a max) or kinetic.

centripetal force.plain: The net inward force for circular motion.

banked curve.plain: A tilted road aiding circular motion.
banked curve.in_class: The normal force's component supplies centripetal force.

concept_sections.heading: Friction
concept_sections.explanation: Kinetic friction opposes sliding with $f_k=\mu_k N$; static friction can grow up to $f_{s,\max}=\mu_s N$ before slipping. Include it in the force balance along the surface.

concept_sections.heading: Uniform circular motion
concept_sections.explanation: Moving in a circle at constant speed still accelerates — toward the center, $a_c=v^2/r$. Some real force (tension, friction, gravity) must supply $F_c=mv^2/r$.
math_steps: Identify what provides the inward force.

concept_sections.heading: Newton's law of gravitation
concept_sections.explanation: Any two masses attract with $F=Gm_1m_2/r^2$ along the line joining them — the same inverse-square form as Coulomb's law.
math_steps: Insert the two masses and separation.
Direction is attractive along the line.

concept_sections.heading: Orbits
concept_sections.explanation: For a circular orbit, gravity is the centripetal force: $GMm/r^2=mv^2/r$. This gives orbital speed $v=\sqrt{GM/r}$ and relates period to radius.

concept_sections.heading: Weight on other planets
concept_sections.explanation: Surface gravity is $g=GM/R^2$, so weight $mg$ changes with a planet's mass and radius even though mass stays the same.

real_world_examples.title: A car rounding a curve
real_world_examples.scenario: Friction keeps a car on a flat curve.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Static friction supplies $mv^2/r$; too fast and it slips.

real_world_examples.title: The Moon's orbit
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Earth's gravity provides exactly the centripetal force for the orbit.

real_world_examples.title: Weight on the Moon
real_world_examples.scenario: Astronauts feel lighter on the Moon.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: $g_{Moon}=GM/R^2$ is about $1/6$ of Earth's, so weight drops.
